slides.title: Who can claim
slides.body: Parents can claim from adult children. A childless senior citizen (60+) can claim from a relative who will inherit their property.

slides.title: Apply to the Tribunal
slides.body: File before the Maintenance Tribunal. It can order interim support and should decide within 90 days of notice. Maintenance is up to ₹10,000 a month.

slides.title: Property and abandonment
slides.body: Gave property on the promise of care, and care stopped? The Tribunal can declare the transfer void. Abandoning a senior citizen is an offence.

caption_instagram:
Caring for elderly parents is not just a duty. In India, it is the law. 👵👴

Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007:

👨‍👩‍👧 Parents can claim maintenance from their adult children; a childless senior citizen (60+) can claim from a relative who would inherit their property
🏛️ Apply to the Maintenance Tribunal; it can order interim maintenance while the case is pending
⏳ The Tribunal should decide within 90 days of notice (extendable once by 30 days)
💰 Maintenance can be up to ₹10,000 a month, as prescribed by State rules
🏠 Property transferred on the condition of care can be declared void if care is refused
☎️ Elderline 14567: toll-free national helpline for senior citizens

caption_linkedin:
India's Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 makes the care of elderly parents a legal obligation, with a simple, quick remedy:

• Parents (biological, adoptive or step) can claim maintenance from their adult children; a childless senior citizen aged 60+ can claim from a relative who possesses or would inherit their property
• The application goes to the Maintenance Tribunal, which can grant interim maintenance while the case is pending
• The Tribunal should decide within 90 days of service of notice, extendable once by up to 30 days in exceptional cases
• Monthly maintenance can go up to ₹10,000, as prescribed by State rules
• If property was transferred on the condition that the transferee would provide care, and care is refused, the Tribunal can declare the transfer void
• Abandoning a senior citizen is an offence punishable with up to 3 months' imprisonment, a fine up to ₹5,000, or both
• Elderline 14567 is the toll-free National Helpline for Senior Citizens
